central_claim: Benton replies that his Fossil Record 2 family analysis still gives no support for periodic spacing of extinction peaks, and defends the data's quality.

Extinction time series from palaeontological databases show self-similar fluctuations with 1/f power spectra (P(f) ~ f^-beta, 0 < beta < 2), supporting the biosphere's nonlinear response as the main mechanism behind the distribution of extinction events.
ambiguity: Framed within self-organised criticality against externally driven periodicity.

central_claim: The self-similarity and 1/f scaling reported by Sole et al. are artefacts of interpolation; uninterpolated extinction records show no fractal scaling.
Extinction and origination rates are uncorrelated at zero lag but correlated at a lag of about 10 Myr, implying a characteristic recovery lag after extinction.
ambiguity: Secondary: the lag persists without the Big Five; intrinsic limits on recovery rate; anthropogenic losses would last millions of years.

central_claim: Spectral analysis shows diversification rates are much less variable than extinction rates at wavelengths shorter than about 25 Myr, implying intrinsic speed limits on how fast diversification can accelerate after extinction pulses.
ambiguity: Secondary: long-wavelength diversification variability equals or exceeds that of extinction.
